title: Image evidence: Paleoindian (about 11,500–10,000 years ago)
summary: Kentucky's first peoples, small mobile family bands who hunted Ice Age animals and later modern game. Almost no human remains or perishable clothing survive from Kentucky, so the picture rests mostly on stone tools and climate data.
displayNote: This picture is an AI illustration reconstructed from the available archaeological evidence for the Paleoindian period in Kentucky; details without direct evidence are informed guesses. AI illustration · Kentucky History Drive.

items.text: [Speculative] No Paleoindian skeletons are reported from Kentucky; build cannot be drawn from local skeletal studies. Show an ordinary, fit adult build without exaggeration.
[Speculative] No direct evidence for hairstyles or ornaments in Kentucky. Keep hair simple (loose or tied back) and avoid invented ornaments.
Hides were scraped and tanned and sewn with bone or wooden needles into clothing, shelters and containers.
[Speculative] Exact garment cut (tailored hide shirt, leggings, cloak for a cold climate) is inferred, not found.
[Speculative] None documented in Kentucky; leave out or keep to a plain cord.
Spear with a fluted Clovis point hafted with sinew; a hide or leather pouch of chert tools such as endscrapers, spokeshaves and gravers.
No atlatl yet in the earliest period; the atlatl is linked to later, smaller points.
Colder climate like Canada's today; evergreen forest and grassland savanna; salt licks such as Big Bone Lick drew mastodons, ancient bison and horse; fluted points found at Big Bone Lick.

A small family group in heavy, plainly sewn hides at the edge of a cold spruce-and-grass savanna near a salt lick in northern Kentucky, one adult knapping a fluted chert point. Gray sky, muted greens and browns, mastodon tracks or distant bison; no feathers, beads or face paint.
